title: Component restriction and graph gluing for nodal Picard groups
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $X/k$ be a connected projective reduced curve with only nodes [def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres, def-kun-projective, def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Give each irreducible component its reduced induced structure and denote it by $X_v$. Its normalization $\widetilde X_v$ [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization] is a smooth projective connected curve. For any such curve $Y$ (including $X$ and $X_v$), let $\operatorname{Pic}^0(Y)$ be the group of invertible sheaves [def-sc-invertible-module] of degree zero after pullback to every normalized component. Let $\Gamma$ be the finite loopless multigraph whose vertices are the $X_v$ and whose edges are the nodes lying on two different components, with those components as endpoints; multiple edges are retained. Choose one orientation of each edge. Set $H_1(\Gamma,\mathbf Z)=\ker(\partial:\mathbf Z^{E(\Gamma)}\to\mathbf Z^{V(\Gamma)})$, with $\partial e=t(e)-s(e)$, where $\mathbf Z^S$ is the free abelian group on the finite set $S$. There is a natural exact sequence of ordinary abelian groups
$$1\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(H_1(\Gamma,\mathbf Z),k^*)\xrightarrow{\iota}\operatorname{Pic}^0(X)\xrightarrow{r}\prod_v\operatorname{Pic}^0(X_v)\longrightarrow1.$$
Here $r$ is restriction and $\iota$ glues the trivial sheaves on the $X_v$ at their intersection nodes, with gluing scalars modulo rescaling on each component. The sequence is equivariant for every $k$-automorphism of $X$: the right action permutes factors and pulls back along component isomorphisms, and the left action is precomposition with the induced signed map on $H_1(\Gamma,\mathbf Z)$. For a connected integral projective nodal curve $Y/k$, $\operatorname{Pic}^0(Y)$ is trivial if and only if $Y\simeq\mathbf P^1_k$.

proof.text: Projectivity implies properness by [lem-pc-projective-proper]. Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-completed-normalization-model] to $X$: it gives finitely many nodes and smooth projective connected normalized components. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-subcurve-boundary] to each reduced component $X_v$: it is nodal and is smooth at every intersection with the complementary reduced subcurve. Thus the only nonsmooth points of $X_v$ are its self-nodes. In particular the same normalization model applies to $X_v$. The graph in the statement is finite and connected: a partition of its vertices with no crossing edge would partition $X$ into two disjoint nonempty closed unions of components. This also checks the asserted normalization and graph conventions.

Put $X'=\coprod_v X_v$, let $v:X'\to X$ be the component map, and let $Z$ be the reduced finite union of nodes on two different components. Over an affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $X$, its inverse image has ring $\prod_vR/I_v$, a finite $R$-module, so $v$ is finite. There is an affine fibre-product square with $Z'=X'\times_XZ$ the disjoint union of two reduced $k$-points per edge. To check this, use [lem-trf-split-node-component-normalization]: at an intersection node there are exactly two minimal primes, one for each branch; use [lem-trf-nodal-subcurve-boundary] to identify their sum with the maximal ideal. Their intersection is zero since the local ring is reduced. The identity $R/(I\cap J)=(R/I)\times_{R/(I+J)}(R/J)$ follows directly by lifting a pair whose difference lies in $I+J$. Hence at that node the local ring is the fibre product of its component rings over $k$. Off $Z$ exactly one component is present and $v$ is an isomorphism. These stalk identities give the sheaf identity $\mathcal O_X=v_*\mathcal O_{X'}\times_{\mathcal O_{Z'}}\mathcal O_Z$, and therefore the affine fibre-product description. The restriction from $v^{-1}U$ to its finite closed reduced subscheme $Z'_U$ is surjective, as a quotient of its affine ring. All hypotheses of the pinching theorem below are now checked.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve), proof at a two-component point; Tag 0C1J (example-glue-points).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-pinching-invertible-patching] to this square over $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Eliminating the one-dimensional node lines from its triples shows that an invertible sheaf on $X$ is precisely a family $L_v$ on $X_v$ and one fibre isomorphism $\lambda_e:(L_{s(e)})_{q_e}\to(L_{t(e)})_{q_e}$ for each edge; morphisms are component maps commuting with every $\lambda_e$. Indeed take the node line to be the source fibre and use $\lambda_e$ for the other identification. Every pair of one-dimensional $k$-spaces admits an isomorphism, so every family $L_v$ lifts. Tensor products multiply the gluing parameters by the tensor compatibility in the cited equivalence. Restriction is therefore a surjective group homomorphism on full Picard groups.

source.place: Tag 0C1M (lemma-glue-points), units-sequence proof, using the rank-one patching formulation.

proof.text: The normalized component maps factor through the inclusions $X_v\to X$. Thus the degree on every normalized component of a glued line bundle is the degree of the corresponding $L_v$. The construction of Step 3 consequently restricts to a surjection $r:\operatorname{Pic}^0(X)\to\prod_v\operatorname{Pic}^0(X_v)$. An element of its kernel admits trivializations of all $L_v$. In such frames its fibre maps are scalars $z_e\in k^*$. By [lem-sc-global-functions], a trivial line bundle on each integral projective $X_v$ has automorphism group exactly $k^*$; each $X_v$ is reduced, proper and connected. Changing the component frames by $a_v$ gives $z_e\mapsto a_{t(e)}z_ea_{s(e)}^{-1}$. Conversely the morphism description of Step 3 says that these are all identifications between trivial-component gluings. Hence $\ker r$ is canonically $(k^*)^E/\operatorname{im}\delta$, injected into $\operatorname{Pic}^0(X)$ by gluing; self-nodes are already part of the component bundles and introduce no extra edge here.

Apply [lem-sfb-finite-graph-cycle-character-quotient] with $A=k^*$. It identifies the quotient in Step 4 with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(H_1(\Gamma,\mathbf Z),k^*)$ by $[z]\mapsto(h\mapsto\prod_ez_e^{h_e})$. Define $\iota$ by the inverse of this isomorphism followed by the gluing injection of Step 4. Its injectivity, image equal to $\ker r$, and surjectivity of $r$ give exactly the displayed short exact sequence, including the one-component and no-edge cases.

source.place: Agent graph-cycle identification of the quotient in Tag 0C1M (lemma-glue-points).

proof.text: Let $b$ be a $k$-automorphism and write $\sigma$ for its permutation of components and intersection nodes. Pulling back a glued sheaf pulls back its component bundles along $b|_{X_v}:X_v\to X_{\sigma v}$ and pulls back its fibre identifications. In the equivalence of [lem-sfb-finite-pinching-invertible-patching], the component and node lines of a sheaf are its actual pullbacks. The commutative squares formed by $b$, its restrictions to $X_v$, and the component inclusions therefore identify the component lines of $b^*L$ with the corresponding pullbacks of $L_v$; the same commuting compositions on each branch identify their fibre maps. This is functoriality of restriction, not an appeal to arbitrary nonflat base-change naturality. On trivial bundles these fibre maps preserve the constant frame $1$. If $b$ preserves the orientation at $e$ the new scalar is $z_{\sigma e}$; if it exchanges source and target it is $z_{\sigma e}^{-1}$. Thus it is $z_{\sigma e}^{\epsilon_e}$. By [lem-sfb-finite-graph-cycle-character-quotient], evaluation on $h$ becomes $\prod_e z_{\sigma e}^{\epsilon_e h_e}=\chi(\sigma_*h)$. This proves both equivariance equations, including the stated precomposition convention, and shows independence of the orientation choices.

source.place: Tag 0C1M gluing construction; automorphism and signed-cycle compatibility supplied explicitly by Q74.

proof.text: For the last assertion apply [lem-sfb-integral-nodal-picard-normalization-action] to the integral projective nodal curve $Y$. If $\operatorname{Pic}^0(Y)$ is trivial, $Y$ has no node: otherwise its injective gluing map $j_q:k^*\to\operatorname{Pic}^0(Y)$ contradicts the existence of a nonidentity element of $k^*$. Such an element exists because an algebraically closed field is infinite (a finite field of size $q$ would have no root of $T^q-T-1$). By [lem-sfb-nodal-completed-normalization-model], normalization is an isomorphism outside the nonsmooth locus, so now $Y\simeq\widetilde Y$ is smooth projective connected. The same cited normalization-action lemma gives surjectivity on degree-zero Picard groups, hence $\operatorname{Pic}^0(\widetilde Y)$ is trivial.

source.place: Tag 0C1M (lemma-glue-points), injectivity when the two branches belong to the same proper component.

proof.text: Write $g$ for the genus of the smooth curve $Y$. Choose a prime $n$ invertible in $k$ ($2$ unless the characteristic is $2$, then $3$). Every $n$-torsion Picard class has degree zero, since degree is the homomorphism to $\mathbf Z$ of [def-sc-pic0] and $n\deg L=0$ implies $\deg L=0$. Thus its Picard $n$-torsion is trivial. But [lem-sc-pic-proper-ntorsion] identifies this group with $(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^{2g}$, which is nontrivial if $g>0$. Therefore $g=0$, and [lem-trf-genus-zero-smooth-proper-line] gives $Y\simeq\mathbf P^1_k$.

source.place: Tag 0C6U (proposition-projective-line); genus detected by prime-to-characteristic Picard torsion.

proof.text: Conversely let $Y\simeq\mathbf P^1_k$. This is a smooth proper connected genus-zero curve by [lem-asd-projective-line-genus-zero]. For a degree-zero line bundle $L$, [sk-thm-picard-rr] gives $h^0(L)-h^1(L)=1$, hence a nonzero section. By [lem-trf-curve-section-degree-positivity], this section has no zero, since a zero would force positive degree. It therefore generates $L$ at every point and identifies $L\simeq\mathcal O_Y$. Thus every element of $\operatorname{Pic}^0(Y)$ is trivial, completing the equivalence.
